questions.question: 1. What is the main purpose of image segmentation in this experiment?

answers.a: To separate foreground pixels belonging to objects of interest from the background
answers.b: To change the image file format
answers.c: To increase the number of pixels in the image

explanations.a: Correct. Image segmentation is used to separate foreground pixels belonging to the object or objects of interest from the background.
explanations.b: Incorrect. File format conversion does not partition an image into regions.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Increasing the number of pixels changes image size rather than separating image regions.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Rotation changes spatial arrangement and does not perform segmentation.

questions.question: 2. Which property is used to characterize the objects considered in this Image Segmentation experiment?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Texture is mentioned as a possible low-level feature, but this experiment restricts the objects considered to brightness.
explanations.b: Correct. In this experiment, objects are defined by their brightness or intensity values.
explanations.c: Incorrect. File size is not used as an image feature for the segmentation methods studied here.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Pixel coordinates identify locations but do not by themselves characterize the object feature used in this experiment.

questions.question: 3. Which segmentation techniques are studied in this experiment?

explanations.a: Incorrect. These techniques are not the two segmentation methods studied in this experiment.
explanations.b: Incorrect. These are morphological operations rather than the two segmentation techniques studied here.
explanations.c: Correct. The experiment studies histogram-based thresholding and region growing for partitioning an image into foreground and background.
explanations.d: Incorrect. These are different image-processing operations and are not the two segmentation techniques studied here.

questions.question: 4. For a single-threshold segmentation with threshold $T$, which condition labels a pixel with intensity $I(x,y)$ as $1$?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This condition does not match the single-threshold rule specified in the experiment.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The thresholding rule does not label a pixel according only to whether its intensity is zero.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The thresholding rule is based on a specific comparison with $T$, not simply on inequality with $T$.
explanations.d: Correct. The experiment defines the single-threshold output so that $I(x,y) \geq T$ is labeled $1$ and the remaining pixels are labeled $0$.

questions.question: 5. A single-threshold approach is most suitable when the image histogram has which characteristic?

answers.a: A bi-modal distribution with two distinct peaks
answers.c: Only one pixel in the image
answers.d: A distribution that is independent of image brightness

explanations.a: Correct. The experiment states that single thresholding is suitable when the histogram is bi-modal, with two distinct peaks.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A histogram with no variation does not provide the two distinct intensity groups described for this approach.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The suitability of thresholding is determined by the intensity distribution, not by having only one pixel.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Threshold selection in this experiment is based on image intensity information.

questions.question: 6. Why can a double threshold be useful when an object of interest has variation in brightness?

answers.a: It removes the need to examine image intensity values
answers.b: It allows a range of intensity values to be selected for the object of interest
answers.c: It always produces the same segmentation regardless of threshold values
answers.d: It changes the spatial resolution of the image

explanations.a: Incorrect. Double thresholding still depends on the intensity values and the selected thresholds.
explanations.b: Correct. Using two threshold values allows an intensity interval to be selected, which can help when the object has some variation in brightness.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The experiment shows that different threshold settings can produce different extracted objects.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Threshold selection changes pixel labeling rather than the spatial resolution of the image.

questions.question: 7. In OTSU thresholding, what quantity is minimized to select the threshold?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The number of pixels is used in the calculation but is not the quantity that OTSU minimizes.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Image width is not the criterion used to select the OTSU threshold.
explanations.c: Correct. OTSU selects the threshold that minimizes the weighted within-class variance of the foreground and background classes.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Spatial distance between pixels is not the optimization criterion described for OTSU thresholding.

questions.question: 8. In region growing, what is the role of the seed pixel?

answers.a: It determines the image file format
answers.b: It is the starting point from which similar pixels are accumulated into the region
answers.c: It automatically determines the histogram threshold
answers.d: It changes every pixel to the same intensity

explanations.a: Incorrect. The seed pixel is used in the segmentation process rather than in file-format selection.
explanations.b: Correct. Region growing starts with a seed pixel inside an object and accumulates neighboring pixels that satisfy the selected homogeneity criterion.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The seed pixel is not used to calculate the automatic histogram threshold in this experiment.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Region growing selects pixels according to a similarity criterion rather than assigning one intensity to the entire image.

questions.question: 9. Which factors are stated in the experiment to have a significant impact on the success of region growing?

answers.d: The seed location, similarity criterion, and selected range

explanations.a: Incorrect. File format is not identified as a factor controlling the success of region growing.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Image dimensions alone are not identified as the determining factors for successful region growing.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The number of pixels alone does not describe the factors identified in the experiment.
explanations.d: Correct. The experiment states that the seed location, similarity criterion, and range have significant impact on the success of region growing.
